item.title: China's top political advisor meets Indonesian People's Consultative Assembly speaker
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-22
Wang Huning, chairman of the National Committee of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference (CPPCC), meets with Ahmad Muzani, speaker of Indonesia's People's Consultative Assembly (MPR), in Beijing, capital of China, Sept. 21, 2026. (Xinhua/Zhang Ling)
BEIJING, Sept. 21 (Xinhua) -- Wang Huning, chairman of the National Committee of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference (CPPCC), met with Ahmad Muzani, speaker of Indonesia's People's Consultative Assembly (MPR), in Beijing Monday.
Wang said the cordial meeting between the two heads of state last year provided new strategic guidance for building a China-Indonesia community with a shared future.
China is willing to work with Indonesia to implement the important common understandings reached by the two heads of state, deepen all-round strategic cooperation, strengthen exchanges of experience in state governance, and bring the building of a China-Indonesia community with a shared future to new heights, Wang said.
The CPPCC National Committee is willing to strengthen exchanges and communication, as well as mutual learning, with Indonesia's MPR, and make greater contributions to advancing the modernization of both countries and the development of bilateral relations, he added.
Muzani said Indonesia highly appreciates China's achievements in economic and social development and regards China as a model to learn from.
Indonesia firmly adheres to the one-China policy and is willing to deepen practical cooperation with China in various fields to better benefit the two peoples, he said.
Indonesia's MPR is willing to strengthen exchanges with the CPPCC National Committee and further promote the in-depth development of bilateral relations, Muzani added.

item.title: Chinese FM urges China, Germany to boost cooperation, uphold free trade
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-22
BEIJING, Sept. 21 (Xinhua) -- Strengthening mutually beneficial cooperation between China and Germany serves the interests of both sides and is the right choice for both, Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi said on Monday.
In a phone conversation with German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul, Wang, also a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, called on China and Germany to send a positive signal of jointly upholding multilateralism and free trade, boost confidence in the development of China-Germany relations, and play a constructive role in the development of China-EU relations.
Noting that China and Germany are major economies in the world and all-round strategic partners, Wang said that in the face of unilateralism and deglobalization, it is necessary for both sides to strengthen strategic communication, enhance mutual trust, and deepen practical cooperation.
The two sides should cherish the progress achieved so far, push China-Germany cooperation to greater depth and solidity, and continue to produce new results, Wang said.
Wang pointed out that the one-China principle is the political foundation of China-Germany relations. He expressed the hope that Germany would cherish and build on the tradition of mutual trust and friendship between China and Germany, adhere to the one-China principle, and take concrete actions to safeguard China-Germany relations as well as peace and stability across the Taiwan Strait, thereby creating the necessary conditions for high-level exchanges between the two sides.
Noting that China and the EU are comprehensive strategic partners, Wang said that the two sides should not fight a trade war.
China has consistently maintained that China and the EU should work in the same direction and resolve each other's concerns through dialogue and consultation, Wang said.
Wang also expressed the hope that Germany would maintain a rational and practical approach, play a positive role within the EU, and help promote the EU to uphold free trade, reject protectionism, and stay on the right course of openness, cooperation, dialogue and consultation.
For his part, Wadephul said Germany-China relations have maintained a sound momentum of development in recent years.
Germany looks forward to further strengthening high-level exchanges with China, holding a new round of Germany-China intergovernmental consultations, deepening practical cooperation in areas such as trade and the economy, and continuously advancing bilateral relations, said Wadephul.
The German side firmly adheres to the one-China policy and the position will not change, said Wadephul.
Noting that the current international situation is facing a series of new threats and challenges, Wadephul said that Germany expects China to leverage its influence in international and regional affairs and work with Germany to explore solutions.
Germany supports the EU and China in properly addressing their differences through dialogue and is willing to play an active role in this regard, he added.
Wang said an important consensus reached by China and Germany today is that China-EU economic and trade issues should be resolved through dialogue and consultation.
The two sides also exchanged views on the situation in Iran and the Ukraine crisis. Wang reiterated China's principled position, saying China will only do what is conducive to peace and remains committed to promoting talks for peace. China stands ready to continue strengthening communication and coordination with the EU and make joint efforts toward this end.

item.title: Fast, focused and forward-looking, China's manufacturing opens new frontier
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-22
* Chinese manufacturers are taking a more targeted approach to global markets, moving beyond standardized products to create solutions tailored to specific needs in different global markets.
* Stronger R&D capabilities and faster responses to market needs are allowing Chinese manufacturers to play a bigger role in product design and development.
* From robotics and embodied intelligence to quantum computing, new applications are opening up a wide range of possibilities for manufacturing and creating new links with markets around the world.
HEFEI, Sept. 21 (Xinhua) -- As Europe was gripped by extreme heat this summer, a production base in Wuhu City, east China's Anhui Province, was racing to meet urgent orders from its European clients: 20,000 mobile air conditioners had to be produced and loaded in just seven days.
The tight deadline set an equally demanding task for the supply chain. More than 1,000 types of components had to be coordinated at the same time, with some rushed to the production line by air and high-speed rail to keep everything on schedule. Once completed, the air conditioners were transported overland across Eurasia to France.
The seven-day turnaround was made possible by a manufacturing system built for rapid shifts in demand -- from adjusting production lines to coordinating suppliers and logistics in real time.
This photo taken on Jan. 6, 2026 shows NIO's 1 millionth vehicle at the NIO Second Advanced Manufacturing Base in Hefei, east China's Anhui Province. (Xinhua/Huang Bohan)
Wuhu is just one part of Anhui's manufacturing landscape. Across the province, manufacturing runs at a scale that can be measured by the minute.
"Every minute, about 190 home appliances, 50 laptops and four new energy vehicles roll off production lines across the province," said Liang Yanshun, Party chief of Anhui, at the ongoing World Manufacturing Convention in Hefei, the provincial capital.
Increasingly, Chinese manufacturers are taking a more targeted approach to global markets, moving beyond standardized products to create solutions tailored to specific needs in different global markets.
TARGETED SOLUTION
In late March, Wuhu-based Tri Waters New Energy Technology Co., Ltd. signed a strategic cooperation agreement with the Maldives' transport authorities to export 32 electric sightseeing boats, each capable of carrying 100 passengers.
Taking into account the Maldives' island geography and demand for greener transport, further plans are in the pipeline to build a photovoltaic energy storage system, charging and battery-swapping networks, and a vessel maintenance base.
"This is a green mobility solution tailored to the Maldives," said Liu Yang, deputy general manager of the company, who noted that the Maldivian side had discussed and planned with the company before reaching a final deal.
Foreign guests learn about vehicles of Chinese automaker Chery at the 2026 Chery International Business Summit in Wuhu, east China's Anhui Province, April 28, 2026. (Xinhua)
"The shift from simply 'taking orders' to 'solving problems' reflects a profound restructuring of the logic of global industrial division of labor," said Han Junhui, an associate researcher at the Chinese Academy of Science and Technology for Development.
For decades, Chinese manufacturers have been engaged in global production networks primarily because of their strong industrial base and cost efficiency, often making products designed by overseas brands, Han said.
"Now, stronger R&D capabilities and faster responses to market needs are allowing Chinese manufacturers to play a bigger role in product design and development," he added.
FORWARD-LOOKING TECH
The same shift is also visible in emerging sectors, where new technologies are still taking shape. From robotics and embodied intelligence to quantum computing, new applications are opening up a wide range of possibilities for manufacturing and creating new links with markets around the world.
At the robotics and embodied intelligence exhibition area of the 2026 World Manufacturing Convention, nearly 200 robots are on display, showcasing applications in logistics, elderly care, services and other fields.
This photo taken on Sept. 20, 2026 shows the robotics and embodied intelligence exhibition area at the 2026 World Manufacturing Convention in Hefei, east China's Anhui Province. (Xinhua/Chang Nengjia)
Data from the General Administration of Customs of China show that China exported more than 12 million robots of various types in the first half of this year, with exports valued at 24.85 billion yuan (about 3.68 billion U.S. dollars), reaching more than 160 countries and regions.
"China has a rich range of application scenarios and a strong manufacturing base. The rapid development of artificial intelligence has further strengthened the competitiveness of Chinese-made robots in international markets," said You Wei, chairman and general manager of EFORT Intelligent Robot Co., Ltd., a robotics manufacturer exhibiting at the conference.
Guo Guangcan, an academician of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, said quantum technology worldwide has accelerated its transition from laboratory research to engineering validation, real-world applications and commercial deployment at scale.
This photo taken on Sept. 20, 2026 shows the LPDDR6 chip at the booth of Chinese memory chipmaker ChangXin Memory Technologies at the 2026 World Manufacturing Convention in Hefei, east China's Anhui Province. (Xinhua/Chang Nengjia)
Hefei has now developed a complete technological system covering quantum chips, cryogenic cooling, measurement and control systems, operating software and cloud services, Guo noted.
Through a quantum computing cloud platform open to users worldwide, its computing services have reached 192 countries and regions, with more than 55 million visits and over 1.16 million scientific research and industrial computing tasks completed.
"These applications have demonstrated the feasibility of commercializing quantum computing at scale and provided a practical path for the global open sharing and cross-sector application of quantum technologies," Guo said.

item.title: GDI has yielded fruitful outcomes over past five years: spokesperson
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-22
BEIJING, Sept. 21 (Xinhua) -- Five years ago today, the Global Development Initiative (GDI) was put forward, and it has yielded fruitful outcomes in implementation over the past five years, Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said on Monday.
Guo said at a regular news briefing the GDI has turned from a Chinese proposal into a global consensus, with the people-centered development philosophy enjoying increasing popularity.
Guo stated that through concrete actions, the GDI has played an enhanced role in advancing global development, mobilizing over 23 billion U.S. dollars and delivering more than 2,000 cooperation projects under the initiative's framework. In particular, practical cooperation under the framework of the Global Development and South-South Cooperation Fund has yielded fruitful outcomes in more than 70 countries, benefiting more than 40 million people, he added.
Guo added that the GDI has developed better cooperation architecture across various sectors, laying the groundwork for advancing international development cooperation as well as realizing the United Nations (UN) Sustainable Development Goals.
Guo stated that the general debate of the 81st session of the UN General Assembly starts on Tuesday. On the sidelines of the general debate, China will host a high-level dialogue on the fifth anniversary of the GDI at the UN headquarters in New York on September 25. "We look forward to working with the broader UN membership to take stock of the achievements and useful experiences over the past five years, share development opportunities, explore cooperation on development, facilitate the implementation of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, and build a community with a shared future for humanity," he said.

item.title: Xi steers China-U.S. relations toward stability
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-22
Chinese President Xi Jinping and U.S. President Donald Trump have a private meeting at Zhongnanhai in Beijing, capital of China, May 15, 2026. (Xinhua/Yan Yan)
BEIJING, Sept. 21 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping is set to travel to Washington for a state visit and a high-stakes meeting with U.S. President Donald Trump.
With the upcoming visit, the two presidents are expected to complete reciprocal visits within months. The trip will be Xi's second state visit to the United States following his first in 2015.
More than a decade on, the world's most important bilateral relationship has followed a bumpy course. How Beijing and Washington manage ties -- and find room to work together -- is increasingly consequential for both countries and the world.
NEW VISION
In May, as Xi hosted Trump in Beijing, he opened their talks with three questions:
"Can China and the United States overcome the Thucydides Trap and create a new paradigm of major-country relations? Can we meet global challenges together and provide greater stability for the world? Can we build a bright future together for our bilateral relations in the interest of the well-being of the two peoples and the future of humanity?"
The questions were raised against the backdrop of years of turbulence in bilateral ties, from trade disputes to tech curbs. Xi has repeatedly stressed the need to find the right way for the world's two major countries to get along.
The Beijing summit gave renewed momentum to that effort. Xi and Trump have agreed on a new vision of building a constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability over the next three years and beyond.
"It marks the first time in more than a decade that China and the United States established a consensus about how to define the relationship that leaders on both sides broadly recognize," said Da Wei, director of the Center for International Security and Strategy at Tsinghua University.
For a while now, China-U.S. relations have moved forward along the track charted by the two leaders. "Head-of-state diplomacy is the anchor of China-U.S. relations," Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi said on Thursday in a phone call with U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio in preparation for the upcoming summit.
Since Trump's re-election, Xi has maintained contact with him through various means, like face-to-face meetings and phone calls, sometimes in a casual format.
During the May visit, Xi invited Trump to Zhongnanhai, the leadership compound in central Beijing, for a private meeting -- an invitation extended to few foreign leaders.
Xi and Trump strolled in the garden, chatting and pausing now and then to admire the towering ancient trees and Chinese roses in full blossom.
Chinese President Xi Jinping welcomes U.S. President Donald Trump upon Trump's arrival at Zhongnanhai in Beijing, capital of China, May 15, 2026. (Xinhua/Li Xiang)
"While President Trump hopes to make America great again, I am dedicated to leading the Chinese people toward national rejuvenation," Xi said later as the two leaders sat down for a conversation over tea.
He urged both sides to keep to the right direction, steer clear of disruptions and promote the steady development of bilateral relations.
Such moments away from the formal meeting table have become a feature of Xi's encounters with Trump, providing a more personal setting to learn about each other's countries and perspectives.
Chinese President Xi Jinping, his wife, Peng Liyuan, U.S. President Donald Trump and First Lady Melania Trump listen as Trump's grandchildren sing a Chinese folk song and recite classics of Chinese literature in the Mar-a-Lago resort in Florida, the United States, April 6, 2017. (Xinhua/Lan Hongguang)
Similar interactions stretch back to Xi's first meeting with Trump in 2017. At Mar-a-Lago, Trump's private estate in Florida, Xi presented him with a piece of Chinese calligraphy bearing an ancient saying: "A nine-story tower rises from a heap of earth; a journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step."
The message carried a metaphor for the relationship Xi hoped the two countries could build. He told Trump that the two leaders could rally those in both countries who shared the goodwill and enthusiasm for advancing China-U.S. relations, and build the edifice of the relationship one story at a time -- making it stronger, taller and more glorious.
BALLAST
Economic and trade relations should continue to serve as the "ballast" and driving force for China-U.S. relations, rather than a stumbling block or a point of friction, Xi told Trump in Busan, South Korea, in 2025. Xi has often likened China-U.S. relations to a giant ship, for which ballast is critical to staying on course through rough waters.
Following the surge of U.S. tariffs in 2025, Beijing responded with resolute countermeasures while continuing negotiations with Washington in an effort to manage their differences. By the time Xi and Trump met in Beijing, their economic and trade teams had reached "generally balanced and positive outcomes."
The dialogue has continued since, with their latest round of talks, which were candid, in-depth and constructive, concluded in New York on Sunday.
There is no winner in a trade war, Xi has repeatedly stressed, both in his exchanges with Trump and on the international stage. "Facts will prove that decoupling and cutting off supply chains will not hold back our development process, and espousing 'small yard, high fences' will only box oneself in and divide the world," Xi said at the just-concluded BRICS summit in New Delhi.
That message also lay at the center of Xi's outreach to the American business community. In March 2024, he met with representatives from U.S. business, strategic and academic communities in Beijing. He told the gathering that the respective success of China and the United States is an opportunity for each other.
During the May visit, Xi sat down with Trump in the Great Hall of the People in Beijing alongside more than a dozen executives from some of America's most preeminent companies, including Apple, Nvidia, Tesla and Boeing.
Trump introduced the business leaders to Xi one by one, underscoring the weight he attached to the delegation.
"Each side, the United States and China, has a big stake in constructive strategic stability," said Robert Lawrence Kuhn, a U.S. scholar and longtime observer of China.
From artificial intelligence and climate change mitigation to public health and counter-narcotics, there are plenty of issues that China and the United States are both involved in, he added.
Rather than expecting Washington and Beijing to suddenly work together perfectly, Kuhn said, the more immediate objective should be to prevent disputes over tariffs, critical minerals, and other issues that could lead to further escalation.
BRIDGING THE PACIFIC
"Friendship, which derives from close contact between the people, holds the key to sound state-to-state relations," Xi has said. For him, the foundation of China-U.S. relations was laid by the two peoples.
Upon the official announcement of Xi's U.S. visit on Monday, his recent reply to American university students was made public. In his letter, Xi encouraged them to foster greater mutual understanding and affinity between people of the two countries, and to promote the steady and sustained development of bilateral relations.
When China-U.S. relations were at a low ebb, Xi cast his eyes toward the future -- young people. The youth, he believes, carry the future and hope of this relationship.
During his 2023 trip to San Francisco for the APEC leaders' meeting, Xi announced an initiative to invite 50,000 young Americans to China for exchange and study programs over the next five years. By May this year, that goal had been reached two and a half years ahead of schedule.
Many participants have written to Xi, thanking him for the opportunity to see China for themselves and forge friendships with their Chinese peers. Xi, in turn, has encouraged young people from both countries to become "envoys of friendship" bridging the Pacific.
A 2026 Reagan Institute Summer Survey found that younger Americans were significantly less likely to view China as a major threat to the United States.
That emphasis on people-to-people bonds extends beyond the younger generation. For decades, Xi has stayed in touch with his old friends in Iowa, whom he first met during his maiden trip to the United States in 1985, and corresponded with veterans of World War II's Flying Tigers, recalling the bonds forged between the two peoples during that time.
"We should build more bridges and pave more roads for people-to-people interactions," Xi once said. "We must not erect barriers or create a chilling effect."
Ahead of Xi's U.S. visit, another story of friendship across the Pacific went viral online.
In 1999, American teacher Ronald Sakolsky donated 5,000 U.S. dollars to support Chinese woman Yin Yuzhen's tree-planting efforts to combat desertification in north China's Inner Mongolia. With the funds, Yin went on to cultivate a forest of more than 50,000 trees.
When Sakolsky and Yin reunited in China in August, he was asked what message he wanted to take home to the United States. His answer was: "Bridge."
He said he believes the upcoming meeting between President Xi and President Trump could help build that bridge.
"China is ready to rebuild the bridge," Sakolsky said. "Is America ready? I believe so."

item.title: Xi replies to U.S. university students
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-21
BEIJING, Sept. 21 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping recently replied to students from 10 U.S. universities who wrote to him after attending youth exchanges in China.
Xi noted that he was delighted to learn that the students enjoyed a pleasant and memorable journey in China.
Xi said he was pleased to hear that the students expressed in the letter their appreciation for Chinese civilization, their hope for friendly cooperation between China and the United States, and their willingness to act as envoys of friendship bridging the Pacific Ocean.
Young people from China and the United States, Xi said, share the same planet Earth and jointly shoulder the mission of the times.
He expressed hope that the students would join the vast number of young people in both countries in striving to carry forward, uphold, and advance China-U.S. friendly cooperation, and work together to foster mutual understanding and affinity between the two peoples and to ensure the steady and long-term development of bilateral relations, so as to contribute the vitality of youth to building a better world.
Recently, nearly 100 students from Harvard University and nine other U.S. universities wrote to Xi, sharing their experiences and what they had gained from the Future Makers 2026 China-U.S. Youth Tour for a Shared Asia-Pacific Future and other exchange events in China, and expressing their willingness to contribute to promoting China-U.S. friendship.

item.title: China's new-generation synchrotron radiation facility achieves first beam
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-21
An aerial drone photo taken on Sept. 16, 2026 shows the Hefei Advanced Light Facility (HALF) under construction in Hefei, east China's Anhui Province. (Xinhua/Zhou Mu)
HEFEI, Sept. 20 (Xinhua) -- The linear accelerator of the Hefei Advanced Light Facility (HALF) successfully generated and delivered an electron beam on Sunday, marking a key step forward in the construction of the world's most advanced fourth-generation synchrotron radiation facility in the low-energy range.
Located in Hefei, capital city of east China's Anhui Province, the institution is a fourth-generation synchrotron radiation facility operating at a designed energy of 2.2 gigaelectronvolts (GeV) and based on diffraction-limited storage ring technology. It is also a major national science and technology infrastructure project in China.
By generating highly intense and coherent light, the facility will serve as a "super microscope" for scientists to probe the microscopic structure of matter.
Compared with third-generation synchrotron radiation sources, HALF is expected to produce soft X-rays with more than 100 times higher brightness and coherence. It will enable the development of experimental techniques with greater precision and sensitivity in the spatial, temporal and energy domains, providing an important research platform for studying microscopic particle behavior, the structure of light elements, and changes in the electronic, chemical and spin states of materials.
This photo taken on Aug. 27, 2026 shows the linear accelerator of the Hefei Advanced Light Facility (HALF) under construction in Hefei, east China's Anhui Province. (Xinhua/Zhou Mu)
"Successful beam generation and delivery means that we have taken a key step toward the ultimate goal. The electron beam produced by the linear accelerator is the source of synchrotron radiation. Its beam quality, stability and reliability directly affect the performance of the storage ring and the downstream beamlines and experiments," said He Zhigang, chief engineer of the injector system.
The project will next enter a critical stage of commissioning, during which the electron beam will be injected into the storage ring. The facility will gradually move toward full-system commissioning and stable operation, He said.
Once completed, HALF will become an internationally advanced fourth-generation synchrotron radiation facility in the low-energy range and complement existing synchrotron radiation sources in China by covering a different energy range. It is expected to provide an experimental platform for cutting-edge research in materials science, life sciences and energy science, and contribute to research in areas including high-temperature superconductivity, new energy batteries, aerospace, biomedicine and advanced materials.
According to He, once completed, HALF will be open to scientists from both China and abroad, providing a shared research platform for advanced studies in fields such as quantum information, energy, environment and life sciences.

item.title: Pinglu Canal opens, creating a new gateway to the sea for southwest China
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-18
On September 16, the Pinglu Canal officially opens to navigation. This 134.2-kilometer canal connects the main channel of the Xijiang River with the Beibu Gulf, giving southwest China a more direct route to the sea.

item.title: Pinglu Canal's Madao Hub Showcases Smart, Green Ship Locks
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-16
A new gateway from China's inland waterways to the sea!
The Madao hub on the Pinglu Canal in Guangxi features giant water-saving locks and smart monitoring systems.
The 134.2-km canal will connect China's inland waterways with the Beibu Gulf, creating a shorter, more efficient route to the sea.
